definition_zh: 约会；预约；任命；委任；职位；职务；（复数）家具设备
definition_en: an arrangement to meet at a fixed time, the act of naming someone to a post, the post itself, or the furnishings of a room
core_image: 日历上圈出的一个时刻，有人在那个点上等你
scene: 诊所前台，护士翻开登记本，在某一页写下一行。 She had an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock.
sceneCN: 这里 appointment 是「约会；预约」（第 1 个义项：约定在固定时间见面的安排）；句意为「她四点与牙医有预约」。画面里有诊所前台、登记本与候诊椅。

pos.zh: 名词：约会；预约；任命；委任；职位；职务

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的动词，义为「任命；约定」
由 appoint 加 -ee 构成，义为「被任命者」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「约定的；被任命的」
由 dis- 加 appoint 再加 -ment 构成，义为「失望」

senses.title: An arranged meeting
senses.definition: an arrangement to meet someone or be at a place at a fixed time
senses.definitionCN: 约定在固定时间与某人见面或到某地的安排
senses.example: She had an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock.
senses.exampleCN: 她四点与牙医有预约。
senses.why: The word carries the French point: a fixed point of time at which two people are to meet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着法语那个「点」：两个人要在某个固定的时间点上见面。

senses.title: The act of naming to a post
senses.definition: the act of officially choosing someone for a job or office
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某项工作或职务的行为
senses.example: His appointment as chief engineer surprised the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他被任命为总工程师，让员工们吃了一惊。
senses.why: The same noun names the act of putting a name at the point of a post.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也命名把名字放到职位这个点上的动作。

senses.title: The post itself
senses.definition: the job or office to which someone has been appointed
senses.definitionCN: 某人被任命担任的工作或职务本身
senses.example: She took up her appointment in the autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 她在秋天就任了这个职位。
senses.why: The point at which the person was placed becomes the place itself.
senses.whyCN: 人被放到的那个点，随后就成了那个位置本身。

senses.title: Furnishings, in the plural
senses.definition: in the plural and in older usage, the furniture and equipment of a room or building
senses.definitionCN: 用于复数且属较古用法，指房间或建筑内的家具与设备
senses.example: The appointments of the old library were sold at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 旧图书馆的家具设备被拍卖掉了。
senses.why: The old sense of furnishing a place survives in the plural, where each object sits at its appointed spot.
senses.whyCN: 布置一个地方的古老义项留在复数里，每件东西都坐在为它指定的点位上。

intro.en: Appointment is appoint plus the noun suffix -ment, and it inherits the French idea of a fixed point.
intro.cn: appointment 是 appoint 加名词后缀 -ment，继承了法语中「固定的一点」的观念。

items.en: Punctum 'a point' comes from pungere 'to prick', and it gives French its word for a point.
items.cn: punctum「点」来自 pungere「刺」，它给法语提供了表示「点」的词。

items.en: Apointer 'to put at a point, arrange' is the verb behind the whole English family.
items.cn: apointer「放到一个点上、安排」是整族英语词背后的动词。

items.en: English appointen appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of arranging or naming.
items.cn: 英语 appointen 在十四世纪出现，带有安排或指定的意思。

items.en: The noun suffix -ment turns the verb into either the act or the thing arranged.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ment 把动词转成动作本身，或转成被安排好的事物。

items.en: The noun covers a diary entry, a named post and, in the plural, the furniture of a room.
items.cn: 这个名词覆盖日历上的一条约会、一个被任命的职位，以及复数形式下的一屋子家具。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on appoint; the near-meaning group gathers words for meetings and posts.
note.cn: 形近组收由 appoint 构成的词；近义组收表示会面与职位的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to name someone or fix a time.
entries.definitionCN: 本词由它加 -ment 构成，义为「任命、约定」的动词。

entries.definition: A person who has been given a post.
To fail to meet a hope or expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使失望」，与 appoint 形近而义远。

entries.definition: Fixed or chosen in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「约定的、被任命的」。

entries.definition: An occasion when people come together.
entries.definitionCN: 人们聚在一起的场合，比 appointment 更不强调事先约定。

entries.definition: A formal arrangement to be somewhere at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 在某个时间到某个地方的正式安排，与 appointment 最近。

entries.definition: A period of time set aside for a particular activity.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项活动留出的一段时间，如诊疗或授课。

entries.definition: A job to which someone is sent, especially abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 被派去担任的职位，尤指驻外职位，对应 appointment 的职位义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a circled point in a diary.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子始终围绕日历上被圈出的那个点。

normal.en: Appoint plus -ment: the thing fixed at a point.
normal.cn: appoint 加 -ment：被固定在某个点上的那件事。

normal.en: A meeting fixed at a point is an appointment.
normal.cn: 固定在某个点上的会面，就是预约。

normal.en: A name fixed at a post is also an appointment.
normal.cn: 固定在职位上的名字，也是任命。

normal.en: The post is the point where the name was placed.
normal.cn: 职位就是名字被放到的那个点。

normal.en: Old furnishings each had their appointed spot.
normal.cn: 旧时的家具各有自己被指定的位置。

abstract.en: One noun holds a time, a job and a room full of furniture.
abstract.cn: 一个名词装着一段时间、一份工作与一屋子家具。

abstract.en: All three are points where something has been fixed.
abstract.cn: 这三者都是某物被固定下来的点。

abstract.en: The word makes arrangement visible as a mark on a page.
abstract.cn: 这个词让「安排」变成纸面上的一个记号。

examples.en: She had an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock.
examples.cn: 她四点与牙医有预约。

examples.en: His appointment as chief engineer surprised the staff.
examples.cn: 他被任命为总工程师，让员工们吃了一惊。

examples.en: The appointments of the old library were sold at auction.
examples.cn: 旧图书馆的家具设备被拍卖掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿波因特门特」——日历上点一个点，写上时间与人名：预约；任命

root: appointment 由 appoint 加名词后缀 -ment 构成。appoint 来自古法语 apointer「放到一个点上、安排」，源头是拉丁语 punctum「点」。因此这个名词的三层主要意思都围绕同一个点：把会面放到时间这个点上，就是预约；把名字放到职位这个点上，就是任命；被放到的那个点本身，就是职位。复数形式还保留了较古的布置义，指一屋子里各就其位的家具设备。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all fix something at a point: a meeting in a diary, a person named to a post, the post itself, and furniture placed in a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都把某物固定在一个点上：日历里的会面、被任命到职位的人、职位本身，以及摆进房间的家具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a time circled in a diary, with a name written inside the circle.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被圈出的一个时刻，圈里写着一个名字。

branches.en: THE DIARY LINE: two people are fixed to one hour.
branches.cn: 日历线：两个人被固定到同一个小时上。

branches.en: THE NAMING LINE: a person is fixed to a post.
branches.cn: 任命线：一个人被固定到一个职位上。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: the fixed point becomes a place to work.
branches.cn: 职位线：被固定的那个点变成工作的位置。

branches.en: THE ROOM LINE: objects each sit at their appointed spot.
branches.cn: 房间线：每件东西都坐在为它指定的位置上。

branches.en: THE ORDER LINE: times and people are arranged into a plan.
branches.cn: 秩序线：时间与人被编排进一个计划。

intro.en: Appointment is a transparent suffix noun, and its stems are all visible inside it.
intro.cn: appointment 是透明的后缀名词，它的各个词干都还能在词里看见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is punctum 'point', which sits behind the French verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 punctum「点」，它位于法语动词背后。

items.meaning: a fixed meeting or a named post
items.example: The appointment was moved to Monday.
They appoint a new coach every year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年任命一位新教练。

items.example: We met at the appointed corner.
items.exampleCN: 我们在约定的街角见面。

items.example: The appointee resigned after a month.
items.exampleCN: 被任命者一个月后辞职了。

items.meaning: forming nouns of act or result
items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It turns the verb into a settled thing.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词转成一件已成定局的事。

items.example: Please make an appointment before you visit.
The gallery is open by appointment.
The receptionist opened the appointment book.
items.exampleCN: 前台翻开了预约登记本。

definition_zh: 长度；长度单位；时长；程度；一段
definition_en: the measurement of something from end to end, its duration in time, the extent to which something is carried out, and a piece cut from something long
core_image: 卷尺从墙角拉到另一头，刻度停在木板的边缘
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉到墙角，低头看刻度，然后在木板上画下一道线。 He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
sceneCN: 这里是「长度」（第 1 个义项：从一端到另一端的量）；句意是他在裁板之前先量了桌子的长度。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、木板、铅笔与墙角。

derivatives.zh: 由 length 加 -y 构成，义为「冗长的；漫长的」
由 length 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「加长；变长」
由 length 与 wise 复合而成，义为「纵向地；沿长度方向」

senses.title: The measurement from end to end
senses.definition: the distance measured along something from one end to the other
senses.definitionCN: 沿某物从一端量到另一端的距离
senses.example: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。
senses.why: Old English lengþu was built from lang plus a suffix of abstract nouns, so the word names the quality a thing has by being long.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lengþu 由 lang（长）加抽象名词后缀构成，所以这个词指的就是事物「长」这一性质。

senses.title: The amount of time something lasts
senses.definition: the period during which something continues from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 某件事从开始到结束所持续的时间
senses.example: The length of the film surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a line with two ends, so the same word for spatial extent is borrowed to measure how long an event runs.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条有两端的线，于是表示空间延展的同一个词被借来量一件事持续多久。

senses.title: The extent to which something is done
senses.definition: how fully or how far an action, argument or piece of writing is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 行动、论述或文章做到多完整、多深入
senses.example: The report discussed the causes at length.
senses.exampleCN: 报告详细讨论了各种原因。
senses.why: Just as a physical thing has a measurable extent, an argument can be carried to a certain extent, which gives the phrase at length its sense of full treatment.
senses.whyCN: 正如实物有可量的延展，一段论述也能被推进到某个「长度」，于是 at length 就有了「充分论述」的意思。

senses.title: A piece cut from something long
senses.definition: a measured piece of rope, pipe or cloth taken from a longer whole
senses.definitionCN: 从更长的整根绳、管或布上截下来的一段
senses.example: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
senses.exampleCN: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。
senses.why: Once length names a measurable extent, a piece that has exactly that extent can itself be called a length, especially in rope and timber.
senses.whyCN: 既然 length 表示可量的长度，那么恰好具有这个长度的一段东西也就能被称为 a length，绳索与木料尤其如此。

intro.en: Length is the oldest English way of naming the quality of being long, formed from the adjective long with a suffix that builds abstract nouns.
intro.cn: length 是英语里指「长」这一性质最古老的说法，由形容词 long 加上构成抽象名词的后缀而来。

items.en: A reconstructed form dlonghos underlies the family of long words, and the same root appears in Latin longus, which is why the two branches look alike.
items.cn: 重构形式 dlonghos 是这一族「长」词的共同来源，同一词根也出现在拉丁语 longus，因此两条分支看起来相似。

items.en: Old English lang meant long in space and in time, and it could also describe a tall person.
items.cn: 古英语 lang 既指空间上的长，也指时间上的长，还能形容人个子高。

items.en: Adding the abstract suffix -þu to lang produced lengþu, the state or measure of being long.
items.cn: 在 lang 后加抽象名词后缀 -þu 得到 lengþu，即「长」的状态或量。

items.en: Middle English respelled the word with th and dropped the old ending, arriving at forms like lengthe.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写改成 th 并丢掉旧词尾，出现了 lengthe 这样的形式。

items.en: Modern English settled on length, kept lengths as its plural, and extended the sense to duration and to a measured piece.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 length，复数 lengths，并把词义扩展到时长与截下的一段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjectives and verbs built on the same long root; the near-meaning group collects words for measured extent and time span.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「长」词根上的形容词与动词；近义组收表示量度延展与时间跨度的词。

entries.definition: Lasting too long or taking more time than needed.
entries.definitionCN: 持续过久或比需要的更费时的。

entries.definition: To make something longer or to become longer.
The adjective from which length was built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 length 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: Distance east or west on the earth, from the Latin word for length.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的东西距离，来自拉丁语中表示「长度」的词。

entries.definition: The space between two points.
The time during which something continues.
The degree to which something reaches or is true.
entries.definitionCN: 某物达到的范围或真实程度。

entries.definition: The full distance or period from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的全部距离或时段。

normalIntro.en: The word is the abstract noun of long, and its family keeps returning to measurement in space, measurement in time and the extent of an action.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 long 的抽象名词，同族词反复回到空间上的量、时间上的量，以及行动的推进程度。

normal.en: Length is long turned into a noun: if a thing is long, its length is the measure of that.
normal.cn: length 是把 long 变成名词：一个东西「长」，它的 length 就是这份长的量。

normal.en: The plural is lengths with th kept, not lengthths, so the spelling adds only an s after the th.
normal.cn: 复数是 lengths，th 保留不动，只在 th 后加 s。

normal.en: Lengthen adds -en to length and turns the measure back into an action of making longer.
normal.cn: lengthen 在 length 后加 -en，把「量」又变回「使之变长」的动作。

normal.en: Lengthy adds -y but carries a hint of criticism: more length than the situation needs.
normal.cn: lengthy 加 -y，却带一点批评意味：长度超过了场合所需。

normal.en: At length means two things at once: after a long time, and in full detail.
normal.cn: at length 同时有两个意思：经过很长时间之后，以及详细地。

abstract.en: The same word measures a table, a film and an argument, which shows how readily English maps time and reasoning onto space.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能量桌子、量影片、量论述，说明英语很自然地把时间和论证都投射到空间上。

abstract.en: A measured piece of rope is called a length, so the abstract measure becomes a concrete object when a knife cuts it.
abstract.cn: 截下的一段绳子也叫 a length，于是抽象的量在刀落下时变成了具体的物。

abstract.en: Long is the adjective of desire and length is its measure, but lengthy is the word we use when the desire has gone on too long.
abstract.cn: long 是表示渴望的形容词，length 是它的度量，而 lengthy 用在「拖得太久」的时候。

examples.en: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
examples.cn: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。

examples.en: The length of the film surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
examples.cn: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「愣是」——这根绳子愣是有三米长；记住 length 是长度。

root: 原始印欧语重构形式 dlonghos（长）→ 古英语 lang → 加抽象后缀 -þu 成 lengþu → 中古英语 lengthe → 现代英语 length；与拉丁语 longus 同出一源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the measure of being long; the senses then apply that measure to time, to how far an action is carried, and to a piece cut to that size.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「长」的量；义项再把这个量用到时间上、用到行动推进的程度上，以及用到恰好截成那么长的一段东西上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape measure stretched from a corner to the far edge of a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺从墙角一直拉到木板的另一头。

branches.en: a tape measure lying along a plank
branches.cn: 沿木板铺开的卷尺

branches.en: a clock face marking a two-hour film
branches.cn: 标出一部两小时影片的钟面

branches.en: a report read slowly, page after page
branches.cn: 一页页慢慢读完的报告

branches.en: a coil of rope cut with a knife
branches.cn: 被刀截断的一盘绳

branches.en: a speaker who finally reaches the point
branches.cn: 终于讲到要点的说话人

intro.en: The word joins the adjective long to an Old English suffix for abstract nouns, and the family then adds endings for quality, action and direction.
intro.cn: 这个词把形容词 long 与古英语的抽象名词后缀接在一起，同族词再加上表示性质、动作与方向的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: measuring much from end to end
items.meaningCN: 从一端到另一端很长的

definition_zh: 每年的；年度的；一年一次的；年刊；一年生植物
definition_en: happening or produced once a year, or calculated over a year; also a plant that lives for one year or a yearly publication
core_image: 日历翻过一整圈，又回到同一个月份
scene: 年底的会议室里，财务把一摞报表推到桌子中央，封面写着年份。 The annual report showed a small but steady rise in sales.
sceneCN: 这里 annual 是「年度的」（第 1 个义项：按一整年计算或每年发布的）；句意为年度报告显示销售有小幅而稳定的增长。画面里有年底的会议室、一摞报表与写有年份的封面。

pos.zh: 形容词：每年的；年度的；一年一次的
名词：年刊；年鉴；一年生植物

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「每年；一年一次地」
由拉丁语 annus「年」加 -ity 构成，义为「年金」，与本词同根
由拉丁语 annus「年」加 vertere「转」构成，义为「周年纪念」，与本词同根

senses.title: Calculated over a year
senses.definition: covering, calculated for, or produced in one year
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖一整年、按一整年计算或在一年内产生的
senses.example: The annual report showed a small but steady rise in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 年度报告显示销售有小幅而稳定的增长。
senses.why: Latin annus is a year, and annuus is yearly: the adjective first marks the span of one full turn of the seasons.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annus 是「年」，annuus 是「每年的」：这个形容词首先标出四季转一整圈的跨度。

senses.title: Happening once a year
senses.definition: happening or held once every year
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生或举办一次
senses.example: The village holds an annual fair in the first week of autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子每年秋天第一周举办集市。
senses.why: A yearly span also supplies a natural rhythm: one event per turn of the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 一年的跨度也提供了天然节律：日历转一圈，事件发生一次。

senses.title: A plant living one year
senses.definition: a plant that completes its life cycle within a single growing season
senses.definitionCN: 在单个生长季内完成整个生命周期的植物
senses.example: Marigolds are annuals and must be planted again each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 万寿菊是一年生植物，每年春天都要重新播种。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for a plant whose whole life fits inside one year.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指那种整个生命都装进一年里的植物。

senses.title: A yearly publication
senses.definition: a book, magazine or report published once a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年出版一次的书籍、杂志或报告
senses.example: The society publishes an annual every December.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会每年十二月出版一本年刊。
senses.why: The thing published on the yearly rhythm borrows the adjective that describes the rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 按年度节律出版的东西，直接借用了描述这个节律的形容词。

intro.en: Annual comes from the Latin word for year, and the whole family is built on the turning of the seasons.
intro.cn: annual 来自拉丁语的「年」字，整个词族都建在四季轮转之上。

items.en: Annus meant 'year', the basic unit of the calendar in Roman life.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，是罗马生活中历法的基本单位。

items.en: The adjective annuus meant 'yearly, of a year', formed directly on annus.
items.cn: 形容词 annuus 意为「每年的、一年的」，直接由 annus 构成。

items.en: Annus plus vertere 'to turn' produced anniversarius, 'returning every year', the source of anniversary.
items.cn: annus 加 vertere「转」产生 anniversarius「每年回转的」，是 anniversary 的来源。

items.en: French annual carried the adjective into administrative and everyday use before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语 annual 把这个形容词带入行政与日常使用，随后英语借入。

items.en: English borrowed annual as an adjective and later made it a noun; exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入 annual 作形容词，后来又把它们名词化；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Finance, gardening and publishing each add a strong everyday sense: annual report, annual plant, annual volume.
items.cn: 金融、园艺与出版各自增加了一个稳固的日常义项：年度报告、一年生植物、年刊。

note.en: The look-alike group is the year family; the near-meaning group gathers words about frequency and duration.
note.cn: 形近组收「年」词族；近义组收表示频率与持续时间的词。

entries.definition: Adverb: once a year or every year.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「每年；一年一次地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A fixed sum paid once a year, especially for a pension or investment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「年金」，指每年支付的一笔固定款项，多用于养老金或投资。

entries.definition: The yearly return of a date, literally a year-turn.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「周年纪念」，字面就是「一年转回来」。

entries.definition: The plainer everyday synonym for annual, with the same two senses.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「每年的、一年一次地」，是 annual 更日常的同义词。

entries.definition: Happening twice a year, not once every two years; the prefix is bi- 'two'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一年两次的」，不是「两年一次」；前缀 bi- 表示「二」，需与 biennial 区分。

entries.definition: A plant that lives for several years, the opposite of an annual.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「多年生植物」，与一年生植物相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin year word, its compounds, and the nouns English made from the adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「年」词、它的复合词，以及英语由形容词造出的名词。

normal.en: Annus is year; annuus is yearly; annual is the English adjective from the same stem.
normal.cn: annus 是年，annuus 是每年的，annual 是从同一词干来的英语形容词。

normal.en: Anniversary is literally a year-turn: annus plus vertere.
normal.cn: anniversary 字面是「一年转回」：annus 加 vertere。

normal.en: An annuity is money that comes back once a year.
normal.cn: annuity 是每年回转的一笔钱。

normal.en: An annual plant lives exactly one growing season; a perennial comes back.
normal.cn: 一年生植物只活一个生长季，多年生植物则会回来。

normal.en: Biannual is twice a year; biennial is every two years. Do not confuse them.
normal.cn: biannual 是一年两次，biennial 是两年一次，不要混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar flipped all the way around and landing on the same month again.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历被整整翻过一圈，又落回同一个月。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of seasons with one marker that passes the same point exactly once each turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个四季围成的圆，有一个标记每转一圈正好经过同一点一次。

abstract.en: Picture a flower that grows, blooms, drops seed and disappears before the year closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵花在一年结束前就长成、开放、落籽、消失。

examples.en: The annual report showed a small but steady rise in sales.
examples.cn: 年度报告显示销售有小幅而稳定的增长。

examples.en: The village holds an annual fair in the first week of autumn.
examples.cn: 这个村子每年秋天第一周举办集市。

examples.en: Marigolds are annuals and must be planted again each spring.
examples.cn: 万寿菊是一年生植物，每年春天都要重新播种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安牛」——安安稳稳一年养一头牛，每年都如此：每年的

root: 拉丁语 annus「年」构成形容词 annuus「每年的」，经法语 annual 进入英语。同一词根还产生 anniversarius「每年回转的」（annus + vertere）与 annuitas「年金」。现代英语由形容词又名词化出「年刊」与「一年生植物」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses follow one full turn of the calendar: a yearly calculation, a once-a-year event, a plant that lives one season, and a publication issued once a year.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项沿着日历转一整圈：按年计算、一年一次的活动、只活一季的植物，以及每年出版一次的刊物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the calendar turns a full circle and returns to the same month.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历转过整整一圈，又回到同一个月。

branches.en: THE SPAN LINE: everything calculated or produced across one year.
branches.cn: 跨度线：在一整年内计算或产生的一切。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM LINE: one event per turn of the calendar.
branches.cn: 节律线：日历转一圈发生一次的事件。

branches.en: THE PLANT LINE: a life cycle that fits inside one growing season.
branches.cn: 植物线：整个生命周期装进一个生长季。

branches.en: THE PUBLICATION LINE: a volume issued on the yearly rhythm.
branches.cn: 出版线：按年度节律发行的一本书或一期刊物。

branches.en: THE SHARED LINE: the yearly span and the yearly event are the same cycle seen as length and as beat.
branches.cn: 共同线：年度跨度与年度事件是同一个循环，一个看成长度，一个看成节拍。

intro.cn: annual 是拉丁语 annus 加形容词词尾 -uus；英语再加 -ly 与名词复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Annus, annuus and anniversarius are recorded Latin words, so this family needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: annus、annuus 与 anniversarius 都是有记录的拉丁词，因此这一词族无需重构。

items.exampleCN: 它是 annual 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms the English adjective annual.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语形容词 annual。

items.example: It joins annus with vertere 'to turn'.
items.exampleCN: 它把 annus 与 vertere「转」接在一起。

items.example: It keeps the yearly money sense.

definition_zh: 定义；释义；清晰度
definition_en: a statement of what a word or idea means; also the sharpness of an image
core_image: 词典上一行小字，把一个词钉住
scene: 她把词典摊在膝上，指尖顺着两行小字往下滑。 The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
sceneCN: 这里 definition 指「释义」（第 1 个义项：说明词义的语句）；句意是词典给出了这个词的两条释义。

senses.title: A statement of meaning
senses.definition: a sentence that says exactly what a word or idea means
senses.definitionCN: 准确说明一个词或概念含义的句子
senses.example: The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给出了这个词的两条释义。
senses.why: A word without a definition is a door without a key.
senses.whyCN: 没有定义的词，就像没有钥匙的门。

senses.title: The act of marking limits
senses.definition: the act of fixing the border or scope of something
senses.definitionCN: 确定某事物的边界或范围的行为
senses.example: The definition of the study area took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 划定研究区域用了一个月。
senses.why: Before a thing can be studied, its edge must be agreed on.
senses.whyCN: 要研究一样东西，先得商量好它的边在哪儿。

senses.title: Sharpness of an image
senses.definition: the clearness of an image or sound on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕上的画面或声音清楚的程度
senses.example: The old film was restored in high definition.
senses.exampleCN: 这部老片子被修复成了高清。
senses.why: A sharp edge is what the eye and the mind both call clear.
senses.whyCN: 边缘锐利，眼睛和脑子都会说它清楚。

intro.en: Definition comes from Latin definitio, a bounding, from finis, a limit, and de-, completely.
intro.cn: definition 来自拉丁语 definitio（划定边界），出自 finis（界限）与 de-（彻底）。

items.en: Finis marked the end of a field or the close of a speech.
items.cn: finis 指一块田的尽头，也指一段话的收尾。

items.en: Definitio was the act of drawing a thing's border.
items.cn: definitio 是给事物画出边界的行为。

items.en: Definicion carried the word into law and learning.
items.cn: definicion 把这个词带进法律与学问。

items.en: English used it for the meaning given in a dictionary.
items.cn: 英语用它指词典里给出的意思。

items.en: Film and screens added the sense of a sharp picture.
items.cn: 电影与屏幕又给它添了画面清晰这一层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fin stem, and the meaning group names what a definition gives to a reader.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fin 词干，近义组则说出定义交给读者的东西。

entries.definition: final and accepted as the best
clear and certain
to say what something means
words that make something understood
what a word or sign stands for

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a finger running down a dictionary and end with a picture sharp enough to touch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从沿着词典往下滑的指尖开始，落到清晰得几乎能摸到的画面。

normal.en: A definition is a small fence built around a large word.
normal.cn: 定义就是给一个大词围起来的一道小篱笆。

normal.en: Two definitions for one word mean two doors into the same house.
normal.cn: 一个词有两条释义，就是同一间屋子的两扇门。

normal.en: You cannot count what you have not first bounded.
normal.cn: 没有先划出范围，就没法数清里面有多少。

normal.en: A high definition picture is just a picture with cleaner edges.
normal.cn: 高清画面，不过是边缘更干净的画面。

normal.en: Definition is the noun that define leaves behind.
normal.cn: definition 就是 define 留下的那个名词。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip stopping under one line of small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖停在一行小字下面。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid on grass to mark where the tent goes.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上拉一根绳，标出帐篷该搭在哪。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf on a screen with every vein in view.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一片叶子，每根叶脉都看得见。

examples.en: The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
examples.cn: 词典给出了这个词的两条释义。

examples.en: By definition, a square has four equal sides.
examples.cn: 按照定义，正方形有四条相等的边。

examples.en: The old film was restored in high definition.
examples.cn: 这部老片子被修复成了高清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definition 记成「定分神」：定得分明，一句话就把词钉住，神都跑了，定义却留下。

root: 源自拉丁语 definitio，出自 definire（划定界限），词根 finis 表示边界与终点。先有「画线」这个动作，才有「划出的范围」，再有「说明词义的语句」；近代摄影与屏幕又借它表示图像的清晰度。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a word, to the act of drawing it, to the edge of a picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 从围住一个词的那条线，到画线的动作，再到画面的边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small fence built around one word.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着一个词搭起的一小圈篱笆。

branches.en: The first sense is the sentence that fences a word.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把词围起来的那句话。

branches.en: The second sense is the act of building that fence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是搭起这道篱笆的动作。

branches.en: On a screen, the fence becomes a clean edge.
branches.cn: 在屏幕上，这道篱笆变成了干净的边。

branches.en: A statement and the act behind it are one thing seen twice.
branches.cn: 一句话和它背后的动作，是同一件事的两种看法。

branches.en: Both senses are about making a shape stand out from its background.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是让形状从背景里站出来。

intro.en: Definition belongs to the finis family, with define, definite, definitive and indefinite beside it.
intro.cn: definition 属于 finis 这一族，旁边还有 define、definite、definitive、indefinite。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: The definition runs to three lines.
The book defines every term it uses.
items.exampleCN: 这本书给每个用到的术语都下了定义。

items.example: We need a definite answer today.
items.exampleCN: 我们今天需要一个明确答复。

items.example: It is now the definitive account.

items.meaning: about the meaning of a term
items.exampleCN: 这场争论是定义上的分歧。

items.example: The law needs a redefinition of duty.
items.exampleCN: 这条法律需要重新界定责任。

items.example: They watched the match in high definition.

definition_zh: 安装；设置；使就职
definition_en: to put equipment or software in place ready for use, or to put someone formally into an office
core_image: 两个人在墙上量好位置，把一台新机器固定牢，插上电
scene: 梯子靠在墙边，工具箱摊开在地板上。 The engineers will install the new heating system before winter.
sceneCN: 这里 install 是「安装」（第 1 个义项：把设备或软件安置好以便使用），句意是工程师会在入冬前安装新的供暖系统。画面里能看到的物件：梯子、工具箱、机器、电线。

pos.zh: 动词：安装；设置；正式任命

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「安装；装置」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「安装者；安装程序」
由本词与 art 构成的复合名词，义为「装置艺术」

senses.title: To put equipment in place
senses.definition: to fix a machine, device, or piece of equipment in position and connect it so that it works
senses.definitionCN: 把机器、装置或设备固定在位置上并接好线，使其能工作
senses.example: They installed a shower in the small bathroom.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在小浴室里装了淋浴。
senses.why: Latin in- "in" plus stallum "a place, a stall": to install is to set something in its proper place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in-「入」加 stallum「位置、座位」：install 就是把东西放到它该在的位置上。

senses.title: To set up software
senses.definition: to copy a program onto a computer or phone and prepare it to run
senses.definitionCN: 把程序复制到电脑或手机上并准备好运行
senses.example: It took ten minutes to install the app.
senses.exampleCN: 装这个应用花了十分钟。
senses.why: The medieval seat became a digital one: the program is put into place inside the machine.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的「座位」变成了数字的：程序被放进机器的位置里。

senses.title: To put someone into an office
senses.definition: to place a person formally in an official position, often with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 以仪式等方式正式把某人安置到官职上
senses.example: The new bishop was installed in the cathedral in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 新主教春天在大教堂正式就职。
senses.why: The oldest sense: a person is seated in a stall, the literal seat of office.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项：人坐进 stallum（座位），即「入座就职」。

intro.en: Install comes from medieval Latin installare "to place in a stall or seat", a church word first.
intro.cn: install 来自中世纪拉丁语 installare「安置到座位里」，最初是教会用语。

items.en: Stallum meant a standing place, a stall, or a seat in a choir.
items.cn: stallum 指站立之处、摊位，或唱诗班的座位。

items.en: Installare "to put into a stall" was used of clergy placed in a prebend or a canonry.
items.cn: installare「放入座位」用于指把教士安置到俸禄或教会职位上。

items.en: Old French installer carried the word into secular use for any placing in office.
items.cn: 古法语 installer 使这个词进入世俗用法，泛指就职。

items.en: English borrowed the verb with the sense "to place" from the fifteenth century, first for church appointments.
items.cn: 英语从十五世纪起用其「安放」之义，最初用于教会任命。

items.en: Industrial and computing usage later extended it to machines and software.
items.cn: 后来的工业与计算机用法又把它扩展到机器与软件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stall place word; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of putting things in place.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stall「位置」这一部分；近义组收其他表示「放置」的动词。

entries.definition: A booth or a stable compartment, the literal place of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摊位、隔间」，是词根字面的「位置」。

entries.definition: The act of installing, or the equipment installed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安装」或「装好的装置」。

entries.definition: A person or program that installs something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安装者」或「安装程序」。

entries.definition: To put a part in place and make it work, common in British speech.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装配」，英式口语常用。

entries.definition: To prepare equipment for use, often on a temporary basis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「设置」，常指临时搭建。

entries.definition: To fix something firmly onto a surface or frame.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「镶嵌、安装」，强调牢固固定在表面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal "seat" inside the word and the objects people install.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词内字面的「座位」，以及人们真实安装的东西。

normal.en: in plus stall: put the thing into its stall.
normal.cn: in 加 stall：把东西放进它的位置。

normal.en: Stall is still a booth; install is seating a machine.
normal.cn: stall 仍是摊位；install 是让机器落座。

normal.en: Install software, then install the printer.
normal.cn: 先装软件，再装打印机。

normal.en: A bishop is installed in a cathedral seat.
normal.cn: 主教的就职是在教堂的座位上完成的。

normal.en: Two l is correct: installed, not installd.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写 l：installed。

abstract.en: Every installation is a promise that the thing will stay put.
abstract.cn: 每一次安装都是一份「它会留着不动」的承诺。

abstract.en: A new habit must be installed like a new boiler.
abstract.cn: 新习惯要像新锅炉一样被装进去。

abstract.en: Installing is a small ceremony of order.
abstract.cn: 安装是一场微小的秩序仪式。

examples.en: We installed new locks on every door.
examples.cn: 我们在每扇门上都装了新锁。

examples.en: The software installs itself in a few minutes.
examples.cn: 这个软件几分钟就自动装好了。

examples.en: He was installed as head of the department last year.
examples.cn: 他去年正式就任部门负责人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬装」——硬要装进去，就是安装

root: 中世纪拉丁语 stallum「站立处、摊位、座位」→ installare「放入座位」→ 古法语 installer → 十五世纪英语。最早用于教会就职，后转指机器与软件的安装。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: fixing equipment, copying software, and seating a person in office.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：固定设备、装软件，以及让人正式就职。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two workers measure the wall and bolt a new machine firmly in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个工人量好墙面，把新机器牢牢固定住。

branches.en: THE WALL: a boiler or camera is fixed and connected.
branches.cn: 墙面这条线：锅炉或摄像头被固定并接线。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: a program is put in its place inside the machine.
branches.cn: 屏幕这条线：程序被放进机器的位置里。

branches.en: THE CATHEDRAL: a person is seated in the stall of office.
branches.cn: 教堂这条线：人被安置到官职的座位上。

branches.en: THE LINK: physical and digital installation share the idea of a proper place.
branches.cn: 连接线：实体与数字安装共享「恰当位置」的观念。

branches.en: THE ROOT: the office sense is the oldest, and the others are echoes of it.
branches.cn: 根源线：就职义最古老，其余义项是它的回声。

intro.en: Install is in- "into" plus the medieval Latin stallum "a place, stall", as a verb installare.
intro.cn: install 是 in-「入」加中世纪拉丁语 stallum「位置、摊位」构成的动词 installare。

latinIntro.en: Stallum and installare are recorded in medieval Latin; the deeper Germanic origin of stallum is not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: stallum 与 installare 有中世纪拉丁语记载，但 stallum 更深的日耳曼来源不属于拉丁语。

items.example: It marks putting into a place.
The verb is the direct source.
Installer names the person or program.
The bare noun survives in English.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的名词仍在英语中使用。

items.example: A different word from the same family.
British usage sometimes drops one l.
items.exampleCN: 英式有时只写一个 l。

definition_zh: 数据；资料（单数）
definition_en: a single piece of information used as a basis for reasoning
core_image: 实验记录本上单独的一行读数
scene: 笔记本上只写了一行读数，却是全部测量的起点。 One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 datum 指「数据」（第 1 个义项：单条资料或数值）；句意是一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。

senses.title: One piece of information
senses.definition: a single fact or figure used as a basis for a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 作为推理依据的单独一条事实或数值
senses.example: One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。
senses.why: The singular keeps its place even when most people say data for one thing.
senses.whyCN: 即使多数人用 data 指一条，单数形式仍守着它的位置。

senses.title: A fixed reference point
senses.definition: a fixed point from which heights or positions are measured
senses.definitionCN: 测量高度或位置时所依据的固定点
senses.example: All heights were taken from the same datum.
senses.exampleCN: 所有高度都从同一个基准点量起。
senses.why: Measuring needs one point that does not move.
senses.whyCN: 要测量，就得有一个不动的点。

intro.en: Datum is Latin for something given, the neuter form of the past participle of dare, to give.
intro.cn: datum 在拉丁语中意为「被给出之物」，是 dare（给出）过去分词的中性形式。

items.en: Dare meant to give, hand over, or grant.
items.cn: dare 意为给出、交出、授予。

items.en: Datum named a thing given, a starting point granted for argument.
items.cn: datum 指被给出之物，即论证时被授予的起点。

items.en: Surveyors used datum for the fixed point of a measurement.
items.cn: 测量师用 datum 指测量的固定基点。

items.en: Scientists took datum into the language of experiment.
items.cn: 科学家把 datum 带进实验的语言。

items.en: The plural data has largely taken over, leaving datum to careful writers.
items.cn: 复数 data 已在多数场合接管，datum 留给讲究用法的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dat- opening, and the meaning group names other single units of knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dat- 开头，近义组则列出其他单个知识单位。

entries.definition: facts collected for use
a particular day of the year
the case of the indirect object
entries.definitionCN: 表示间接宾语的语法格

entries.definition: something known to be true
a number that records an amount
a single number taken from a set of records
entries.definitionCN: 从一组记录中取出的单个数字

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one line in a notebook and end with a surveyor's fixed mark in the ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笔记本上的一行字开始，落到测量员钉在地里的固定标记。

normal.en: One datum is a stone; data is the wall built from it.
normal.cn: 一个数据是一块石头，数据是一堵用石头砌成的墙。

normal.en: The word means given, because a fact is handed to you before you reason.
normal.cn: 这个词意为「被给出」，因为事实总在你推理之前就被递到手上。

normal.en: Keep the singular and you keep the habit of counting carefully.
normal.cn: 守住单数，就守住了仔细计数的习惯。

normal.en: Every measurement needs one point that refuses to move.
normal.cn: 每次测量都需要一个不肯移动的点。

normal.en: Datum is the word a careful engineer still writes in a report.
normal.cn: 严谨的工程师在报告里仍然会写 datum。

abstract.en: Picture a single number underlined twice in a lab book.
abstract.cn: 想象实验本上一个被划了两道线的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a brass pin set in concrete before any building starts.
abstract.cn: 想象动工之前，一枚铜钉被嵌进混凝土。

abstract.en: Picture one dot on a graph with nothing else drawn yet.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上只画了一个点，别的都还没有。

examples.en: One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
examples.cn: 一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。

examples.en: All heights were taken from the same datum.
examples.cn: 所有高度都从同一个基准点量起。

examples.en: Each datum in the table was checked twice.
examples.cn: 表格里的每一条数据都核对了两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 datum 记成「得Ta」：得（dei）到一个答案，靠的就是这一条数据。

root: 拉丁语 datum 意为「被给出之物」，是 dare（给出）的过去分词中性形式，最初指论证前已被授予的起点；十七世纪进入英语测量术语，指固定基准点，十八世纪起成为实验与统计中单个事实或数值的名称。

sensesIntro.en: From one given fact, to the fixed point from which all measuring starts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被给出的一条事实，到一切测量所依据的那个定点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one underlined number in a notebook of measurements.
core.cn: 核心意象：测量笔记本里一个画了线的数字。

branches.en: The first sense is the smallest unit of evidence.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是证据的最小单位。

branches.en: The second turns the unit into a point in space.
branches.cn: 第二个把这个单位变成空间中的一个点。

branches.en: Both senses need something given before anything can be built.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有「被给出的东西」，才能开始搭建。

branches.en: A surveyor's mark is itself one datum among many.
branches.cn: 测量员的标记本身也是众多数据中的一条。

branches.en: The word keeps asking where the figure came from.
branches.cn: 这个词始终在问：这个数字是从哪里来的。

intro.en: Datum is the singular trunk from which data, database, and databank all branch.
intro.cn: datum 是主干单数，data、database 与 databank 都从它分枝出去。

latinIntro.en: The Latin participle datum, given, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语分词 datum（被给出的）是整个词族的源头。

items.example: A single datum cannot prove the theory.
items.exampleCN: 一个数据无法证明这个理论。

items.example: The database holds ten years of records.
items.exampleCN: 这个数据库存着十年的记录。

items.example: The databank is open to researchers.

items.meaning: the fixed point of a survey
items.example: They set a datum point on the hill.
items.exampleCN: 他们在山上设了基准点。

items.meaning: the line drawn from that point
the surface used as a base

items.example: Each raw datum went into the file.
items.exampleCN: 每条原始数据都进了档案。

latinEntries.example: Dare is the verb behind datum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: dare 是 datum 背后的动词。

definition_zh: 大量的；坚固的；实质的
definition_en: large in amount or importance, or solid and strong
core_image: 一大块沉甸甸、能撑住东西的实体
scene: 这项工程需要大量资金。 The project requires a substantial amount of money.
sceneCN: 这里 substantial 是「大量的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这项工程需要大量资金。

senses.title: Large in amount
senses.definition: large in size, amount, or value
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、数量或价值上很大
senses.example: The project requires a substantial amount of money.
senses.exampleCN: 这项工程需要大量资金。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Solid
senses.definition: strong and solidly built
senses.definitionCN: 结实坚固的
senses.example: The table is made of substantial wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子是用结实的木料做的。
senses.why: The original sense is physical solidity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的本义就是物理上的坚实。

senses.title: Real
senses.definition: real and important rather than slight
senses.definitionCN: 真实而重要，而非轻微的
senses.example: They made substantial progress this year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们今年取得了实质性进展。
senses.why: Solidity becomes importance.
senses.whyCN: 坚实引申为重要。

intro.en: Substantial comes from substance plus an adjective ending.
intro.cn: substantial 由 substance 加形容词后缀构成。

items.en: Substantia meant what stands beneath.
items.cn: substantia 意为站在下面的东西。

items.en: Substantialis meant having substance.
items.cn: substantialis 意为有实体的。

items.en: Substantiel described something solid.
items.cn: substantiel 形容坚实的东西。

items.en: Substantial described solid things.
items.cn: substantial 形容坚固之物。

items.en: Substantial widened to mean large.
items.cn: substantial 扩展为表示大量的。

note.en: Substantial is compared with look-alike words and with words for large.
note.cn: 把 substantial 与形近词以及表示大量的词作比较。

entries.definition: acting as a replacement
thin and weak
based on indirect evidence
large in amount
important or large enough to matter
hard and firm

normalIntro.en: Substantial is something with real weight, in the hand or in the numbers.
normalIntro.cn: substantial 是有分量的东西，无论拿在手里还是写在数字里。

normal.en: The project requires a substantial amount of money.
normal.cn: 这项工程需要大量资金。

normal.en: The table is made of substantial wood.
normal.cn: 这张桌子是用结实的木料做的。

normal.en: They made substantial progress this year.
normal.cn: 他们今年取得了实质性进展。

normal.en: She gave a substantial meal to the guests.
normal.cn: 她给客人做了一顿丰盛的饭。

normal.en: There is substantial evidence for the claim.
normal.cn: 这一说法有确凿证据。

abstract.en: Substantial things leave a mark when they are moved.
abstract.cn: 有分量的东西，移动时会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: A substantial silence can say more than a speech.
abstract.cn: 沉甸甸的沉默，可能比讲话说得更多。

abstract.en: What is substantial does not need to shout.
abstract.cn: 真正有分量的东西，不必大声嚷嚷。

examples.en: The project requires a substantial amount of money.
examples.cn: 这项工程需要大量资金。

examples.en: The table is made of substantial wood.
examples.cn: 这张桌子是用结实的木料做的。

examples.en: There is substantial evidence for the claim.
examples.cn: 这一说法有确凿证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: substantial 是「大量的、坚固的、实质的」；substantial amount 是大量，substantial increase 是大幅增长，substantial evidence 是确凿证据。

root: 由 substance（物质、实体）加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，字面是「有实体的」；由物理上的坚实，引申为数量上的大量和意义上的重要、实质。

sensesIntro.en: Substantial means large in amount, solidly built, or real and important.
sensesIntro.cn: substantial 表示数量大、结构坚固，或真实重要。

core.en: A solid mass that takes up real space.
core.cn: 占据真实空间的一团实体。

branches.en: The project requires a substantial amount of money.
branches.cn: 这项工程需要大量资金。

branches.en: The table is made of substantial wood.
branches.cn: 这张桌子是用结实的木料做的。

branches.en: They made substantial progress this year.
branches.cn: 他们今年取得了实质性进展。

branches.en: Solid build and large amount share the idea of weight.
branches.cn: 坚固的构造和巨大的数量，共享「分量」这一意象。

branches.en: What is solid becomes what is important.
branches.cn: 坚实的东西，逐渐成为重要的东西。

intro.en: Substantial takes -ly and pairs with the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: substantial 可加 -ly，并与否定前缀 in- 组合。

definition_zh: 以某种方式；不知怎么地
definition_en: in a way that is not known or not stated
core_image: 一辆旧车摇摇晃晃，却还是开到了山顶
scene: 我们总能想办法把箱子搬上楼。 We will get the box upstairs somehow.
sceneCN: 这里 somehow 是「以某种方式」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们总能想办法把箱子搬上楼。

pos.zh: 不知怎么地；莫名其妙地

senses.title: By some means
senses.definition: in a way that is not stated but is possible
senses.definitionCN: 以没有说明但可行的某种方式
senses.example: We will get the box upstairs somehow.
senses.exampleCN: 我们总能想办法把箱子搬上楼。
senses.why: Some plus how names a method left unnamed.
senses.whyCN: some 加 how，指一种没有说出的方法。

senses.title: For no clear reason
senses.titleCN: 不知怎么地；莫名其妙地
senses.definition: for a reason that is not known or understood
senses.definitionCN: 出于不知道或不理解的原因
senses.example: Somehow I knew she would call.
senses.exampleCN: 不知怎么地，我就知道她会打电话来。
senses.why: An unnamed way can also be an unexplained cause.
senses.whyCN: 未说明的方式，也可以指未解释的原因。

intro.en: Somehow joins some with the old word how.
intro.cn: somehow 把 some 与古老的 how 组合在一起。

items.en: Sum meant some; hu meant how.
items.cn: sum 意为一些，hu 意为如何。

items.en: The compound named an unnamed manner.
items.cn: 这个复合词指一种未说明的方式。

items.en: It came to mean by one means or another.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示「用这样或那样的办法」。

items.en: It also came to mean for an unknown reason.
items.cn: 它也开始表示「出于未知的原因」。

items.en: The phrase somehow or other fixed the first sense.
items.cn: somehow or other 这一说法固定了第一个义项。

note.en: Somehow is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of unspecified manner.
note.cn: 把 somehow 与形近词以及表示不确定方式的副词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Somehow says a way exists even when no one can name it.
normalIntro.cn: somehow 表示：即使没人说得出方法，办法仍然存在。

normal.en: We will get the box upstairs somehow.
normal.cn: 我们总能想办法把箱子搬上楼。

normal.en: Somehow I knew she would call.
normal.cn: 不知怎么地，我就知道她会打电话来。

normal.en: They somehow finished before noon.
normal.cn: 他们不知怎么在中午前完成了。

normal.en: Somehow or other, the door opened.
normal.cn: 不管怎样，门还是开了。

normal.en: He somehow found the lost ring.
normal.cn: 他不知怎么就找到了丢失的戒指。

abstract.en: Somehow is hope wearing the clothes of method.
abstract.cn: somehow 是穿上了方法外衣的希望。

abstract.en: Naming no way keeps every way open.
abstract.cn: 不说出办法，就是让所有办法都还敞开着。

abstract.en: The unexplained is not the impossible.
abstract.cn: 无法解释的，并不等于不可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: somehow 是 some（某个）加 how（如何）：说不清「如何」，就用 somehow；somehow or other 是「不管怎样」，意思与 anyhow 接近。

root: 由 some（某个）与 how（如何）组合而成，核心义「以某种未说明的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Somehow means by an unnamed means, or for an unknown reason.
sensesIntro.cn: somehow 意为以未说明的方式，或出于未知的原因。

core.en: A way or cause that is left unnamed.
core.cn: 一种未说明的方式或原因。

branches.en: A heavy box still reaches the top floor.
branches.cn: 沉重的箱子还是被弄上了顶楼。

branches.en: A phone rings just before it is expected.
branches.cn: 电话恰在预料之前响起。

branches.en: An unnamed method and an unnamed cause share one word.
branches.cn: 未说明的方法与未说明的原因共用一个词。

branches.en: Somehow or other leaves all methods open.
branches.cn: somehow or other 把所有方法都保留着。

branches.en: What cannot be explained can still be done.
branches.cn: 解释不了的事，照样能做到。

intro.en: Somehow belongs to the some- family of unnamed ways and places.
intro.cn: somehow 属于由 some 构成、表示未知方式与地点的词族。

latinIntro.en: Somehow has no Latin root; both parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: somehow 没有拉丁词根，两部分都来自古英语。

definition_zh: 拒绝；否决；排斥；次品
definition_en: to refuse to accept an offer, an idea, or a person; to turn down an application officially; to attack a transplanted organ; a thing thrown out as imperfect
core_image: 一份申请被推回桌边，上面盖着红色的退回章
scene: 窗口里的工作人员看了一眼材料，盖章后把它推回桌边。 The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
sceneCN: 这里 rejected 是 reject 的过去式，取「否决」（第 2 个义项：正式驳回一项提议）；句意为委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。画面里可留意：被推回的材料、红色的退回章。

senses.title: To refuse to accept
senses.definition: to say no to something offered or proposed
senses.definitionCN: 对提供或提议之物说不
senses.example: She rejected the job because it meant moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝了这份工作，因为那意味着要移居国外。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to throw back: an offer is cast back to the hand that held it out.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「扔回去」：提议被抛回伸出它的那只手。

senses.title: To turn down officially
senses.definition: to refuse an application, a plan, or a proposal through a formal decision
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式决定驳回申请、计划或提案
senses.example: The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。
senses.why: A formal no is still a throwing back, but now the throw is made on behalf of an office and recorded.
senses.whyCN: 正式的「不」仍是扔回去，只是这一扔代表一个机构，并被记录下来。

senses.title: To attack transplanted tissue
senses.definition: of a body, to refuse to accept transplanted tissue and attack it
senses.definitionCN: 指身体不接受移植组织并加以攻击
senses.example: Her body rejected the new kidney within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她的身体在一周内就排斥了新的肾脏。
senses.why: The body throws back what it does not recognise as its own, which is the same gesture at the scale of cells.
senses.whyCN: 身体把不认作自身的东西扔回去，这是同一动作在细胞尺度上的表现。

intro.en: Reject is a throwing back: the Latin verb joins a prefix of return to the verb to throw.
intro.cn: reject 是「扔回去」：这个拉丁动词把表返回的前缀接在「投掷」动词上。

items.en: Iacere meant to throw or cast, and it underlies many English verbs of sending.
items.cn: iacere 意为投掷或抛出，是许多英语「送出」类动词的基础。

items.en: Reicere joined re-, back, with iacere and meant to throw back or cast off.
items.cn: reicere 由 re-（往回）与 iacere 组成，意为扔回去或抛开。

items.en: The participle reiectus meant thrown back, and it gave the noun and the adjective their shape.
items.cn: 分词 reiectus 意为被扔回的，名词与形容词的形式都由此而来。

items.en: French rejecter meant to refuse or cast aside, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 rejecter 意为拒绝或抛开，英语即以此义借入。

items.en: Modern medicine applied the word to a body casting off transplanted tissue.
items.cn: 现代医学把这个词用于身体排除移植组织的现象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the Latin verb to throw; the near-meaning group gathers words for refusing.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁「投掷」动词构成的动词；近义组收表示拒绝的词。

To throw forward or plan.
To throw out.
To say no to something.

To throw away as useless.

normalIntro.en: The word is a throw: an offer, a plan, or a piece of tissue is sent back where it came from.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次投掷：提议、方案或一块组织，被送回它来的地方。

normal.en: Re plus iacere, back plus throw: to throw an offer back.
normal.cn: re 加 iacere，往回加扔：把提议扔回去。

normal.en: A committee rejects a plan with a vote, not a shrug.
normal.cn: 委员会用投票否决方案，而不是耸耸肩。

normal.en: A body rejects a transplant because it reads it as foreign.
normal.cn: 身体排斥移植器官，因为它把那读作异物。

normal.en: Rejection is the noun, and it hurts more than the verb.
normal.cn: rejection 是名词，它比动词更伤人。

normal.en: Do not confuse reject with eject, which throws something out for good.
normal.cn: 别把 reject 与 eject 弄混，后者是把东西彻底抛出。

abstract.en: To reject an idea is not to have heard it.
abstract.cn: 否决一个想法，并不等于听懂了它。

abstract.en: Every rejection is a decision about what a group will not become.
abstract.cn: 每一次拒绝，都是一个群体关于「不成为什么」的决定。

abstract.en: A body that rejects a gift is only protecting its own outline.
abstract.cn: 排斥外来物的身体，只是在守住自己的轮廓。

examples.en: The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
examples.cn: 委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。

examples.en: She rejected the job because it meant moving abroad.
examples.cn: 她拒绝了这份工作，因为那意味着要移居国外。

examples.en: Her body rejected the new kidney within a week.
examples.cn: 她的身体在一周内就排斥了新的肾脏。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 ject（扔）：把递来的提议扔回去，是拒绝；把方案扔回去，是否决；把移植物扔回去，是排斥。

root: 拉丁 iacere（投掷）→ reicere（扔回去）→ reiectus（被扔回的）→ 法语 rejecter → 英语 reject；同族有 rejection、rejective，形近的 inject、project、eject 共用 iacere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is throwing back; the senses move from refusing an offer, to an official no, to a body casting off foreign tissue.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「扔回去」；义项从拒绝提议，到正式的否决，再到身体排除外来组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an application pushed back across a counter under a red stamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份申请被推回桌边，上面盖着红色的退回章。

branches.cn: 被投票否决的方案

branches.en: a kidney the body will not keep
branches.cn: 身体不肯留下的肾脏

branches.cn: 提议与方案都被送回

branches.cn: 委员会与身体都在说不

intro.en: A Latin verb of throwing takes a prefix of return, and the compound moves from arrows to offers and finally to cells.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「投掷」动词接上表返回的前缀，这个复合词从箭矢走到提议，最后走到细胞。

latinIntro.en: The base is iacere, to throw; re- means back, and the participle reiectus feeds the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 iacere（投掷）；re- 表「往回」，分词 reiectus 供给名词形式。
